transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. [Name], nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?
Mostly, I’m here because I’m tired in a way that sleep doesn’t seem to fix. Even small things, like unloading the dishwasher or reading for my certificate class, can feel like too much.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, or has it been going on for months?
About four months, I think. It started around when the arguments with my spouse got a lot more frequent.
Over the past four months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?
Yeah. I’ve kind of stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself—sketching, gallery openings, cooking, yoga, even playing tennis with a friend.
Even on nights when you get a full night's sleep, do you wake up still feeling exhausted or unrefreshed?
Yes. Even if I sleep through the night, I wake up feeling like I haven’t really rested. Small things like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my class can feel like too much.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or that you seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you're asleep?
I’m not sure. No one’s mentioned that to me.
Over these past four months, have you noticed any unintentional weight gain or weight loss?
I think I’ve lost some weight without meaning to. My appetite’s been off—I’ll sometimes just have coffee and a few bites of food all day, and my jeans have gotten looser.
Have you noticed you're feeling unusually thirsty or needing to urinate more often than usual over these past few months?
I haven’t really noticed being thirstier than usual or needing to use the bathroom more often.
Over these past four months, have you been feeling unusually guilty or like you're worthless or a burden to others?
I haven’t really been feeling guilty or like I’m worthless or a burden.
Over these past four months, have you found yourself worrying excessively about various things, and do you feel like you can't control or stop that worry?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a lot of worrying that I can’t stop.
Over the past four months, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling down or hopeless most days.
Have you noticed feeling unusually short of breath, dizzy, or lightheaded, especially with physical activity, over these past few months?
I’m not sure—I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Have you or anyone else noticed that your skin, lips, or nail beds look unusually pale, or do you find yourself feeling cold more often than before?
No, I haven’t noticed my skin or lips looking pale, and I don’t think I’ve been feeling colder than usual.
Do you find yourself needing to nap during the day or struggling to stay awake during activities, even after sleeping a full night?
Yeah, sometimes. Even if I’ve slept, I’m still just really tired—small things like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class can feel like too much.
Over these past four months, have you noticed it's harder than usual to concentrate, think clearly, or make decisions?
Yeah, I think so. I’ll open my planning app and just stare at it—not able to decide if I should do a class assignment, pay a bill, or start dinner. Then I end up not doing any of it for a while.
Have you ever had a similar period in the past—weeks or months of feeling this exhausted, unmotivated, and uninterested in things you normally enjoy—before this current episode?

Yeah. I’ve had periods before where I just stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself—sketching, going to gallery openings, cooking, yoga, even playing tennis with a friend.
Between those past episodes and now, did you go back to feeling like your normal self for weeks or months at a time, or has this low, tired feeling always been there to some degree?
I’m not really sure. I know there have been times I felt more like myself, but I can’t say exactly how long those stretches lasted.
Thinking back to that earlier time you mentioned feeling this way, do you recall if it lasted for at least two weeks or more?
I’m not sure, honestly. I remember it being more than just a few bad days, but I can’t really say whether it was two weeks or longer.
When you do take a nap during the day, do you wake up feeling refreshed, or still just as tired as before?
Still tired, really. The nap doesn’t seem to fix it. Even afterward, something small like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class can feel like too much.
On a typical night, about how many hours do you sleep in total?
I’m not sure exactly. I haven’t really kept track of how many hours I sleep on a typical night.
Do you find that you're sleeping notably longer than you used to—for example, more than 9 or 10 hours in a 24-hour period, including naps?
I really couldn’t say. I haven’t noticed or kept track of whether it adds up to that much in a day.
